notes: Pilot only. No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional — not absolute anatomy. No Travell verbatim text.

relations.source_structure: cervical nerve root / cervical somatic structures (C5–C6 pathway)
relations.clinical_context: Lateral shoulder pain with neck symptoms, dermatomal/myotomal clues, or poor reproduction on local cuff tests.
supporting_evidence: Cervical radiculopathy clusters (Wainner) support cervical contribution when present
Cross-region screening is standard when local tests fail to reproduce familiar pain

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Spurling more specific than sensitive; negative Spurling does not exclude cervical contribution.

limitations: Cervical contribution and RCRSP often coexist
Do not label as 'cervical confirmed' from one test
recommended_examination: Cervical AROM + Spurling / distraction / ULTT as cluster
Ask if neck movement changes shoulder pain
Repeat local cuff cluster for familiar pain

references.citation: Wainner RS et al. Reliability and diagnostic accuracy of the clinical examination and patient self-report measures for cervical radiculopathy. Spine. 2003.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT. 2017.

relations.source_structure: rotator cuff / subacromial complex (clinical RCRSP construct)
relations.clinical_context: Isolated Neer or Hawkins negative (or non-familiar pain) while history still suggests load-related lateral shoulder pain.
supporting_evidence: Impingement tests have limited diagnostic accuracy in isolation
Prefer cluster + familiar pain rather than single-test exclusion

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent numeric Sn/Sp. Literature shows mixed/limited standalone accuracy (Hegedus reviews; Lewis RCRSP framing).

limitations: Technique, irritability, and familiar-pain criterion matter
recommended_examination: Painful arc + Jobe/Full Can with familiar pain
Cervical screen if local cluster weak

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Physical examination tests of the shoulder: a systematic review with meta-analysis of individual tests. Br J Sports Med.
Lewis J. Rotator cuff related shoulder pain: Assessment, management and uncertainties. Man Ther / related RCRSP papers.

relations.clinical_context: When cuff special tests are inconclusive and palpation reproduces familiar pain in infraspinatus region — treat as hypothesis only.
supporting_evidence: Classical myofascial referral maps describe lateral shoulder patterns from scapular muscles (traditional class)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Palpation reliability for MTrP is limited; MTrP found ≠ proven cause.

limitations: Traditional maps are not absolute anatomy
High methodological controversy in MTrP diagnosis
recommended_examination: Reproduce familiar pain with palpation + movement tests
Compare with cuff and cervical clusters
Reassess if no change after local treatment

references.citation: Tough EA et al. Variability of criteria used to diagnose myofascial trigger point pain syndrome — evidence of limited reliability/validity concerns in the MTrP literature (use as caution, not atlas).
Lucas N, Macaskill P, Irwig L, Moran R, Bogduk N. Reliability of physical examination for diagnosis of myofascial trigger points. Clin J Pain. 2009.

relations.clinical_context: Pain more at the point of the shoulder or with cross-body load; may be labelled 'lateral' by the patient.
supporting_evidence: AC pain is a clinical construct overlapping RCRSP
Isolated special tests have limited standalone accuracy (qualitative)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp for cross-body or AC palpation.

recommended_examination: Localized AC palpation with familiar pain

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Physical examination tests of the shoulder: systematic review with meta-analysis. Br J Sports Med — qualitative: isolated tests mixed/limited.
Lewis J. Rotator cuff related shoulder pain — overlapping anterior/superior constructs.

relations.source_structure: cardiac / visceral (ACS and related chest-pain pathways)
relations.clinical_context: Shoulder or arm pain with chest pressure, dyspnoea, diaphoresis, nausea, exertional pattern, or vascular risk — not a physiotherapy special test.
supporting_evidence: Chest-pain guidelines require urgent medical pathway when ACS features are present
MSK hypothesis must wait until safety is addressed

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Safety pathway, not a diagnostic accuracy claim for a physio test.

limitations: Not all referred shoulder pain is cardiac
Do not delay emergency care to complete an MSK cluster
recommended_examination: Stop elective MSK cascade if ACS/visceral features present
Urgent medical referral per local pathway
red_flags: Pain into arm/jaw with exertional or autonomic features

references.citation: Gulati M et al. 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain. Circulation/JACC. 2021.

relations.target_region: shoulder girdle / scapular / lateral shoulder perceived pain
relations.clinical_context: Shoulder-girdle pain that changes with cervical movement; local cuff tests poorly reproduce familiar pain.
supporting_evidence: Fluoroscopy-controlled zygapophyseal provocation in volunteers and patients can refer to the shoulder girdle
Does not identify the exact segment from pain location in clinic

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: These studies map referred patterns under provocation; they are not Sn/Sp of Spurling or palpation.

limitations: Must not be used as Travell-style muscle maps
recommended_examination: Ask whether neck movement changes shoulder pain
Do not diagnose a facet level from a pain drawing

references.citation: Dwyer A, Aprill C, Bogduk N. Cervical zygapophyseal joint pain patterns. I: A study in normal volunteers. Spine. 1990.
Aprill C, Dwyer A, Bogduk N. Cervical zygapophyseal joint pain patterns. II: A clinical evaluation. Spine. 1990.
Fukui S et al. Referred pain distribution of the cervical zygapophyseal joints and cervical dorsal rami. Pain. 1996.
